RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 50

An all-male panel often reflects senior industry demographics rather than overt discrimination, though homogeneous panels carry a known risk of affinity or unconscious bias. The gap in technical experience (15 versus 8 years) raises reasonable questions, but leadership appointments also heavily weigh client relationships, commercial strategy, and interview impressions.

Raising the panel's gender composition directly right now risks provoking defensiveness and burning bridges before you have facts. Instead, follow up professionally on your request for written feedback. Focus on objective criteria and why the other candidate was preferred. If the response is evasive, inconsistent, or suggests unlawful bias, consult an employment lawyer or HR specialist to evaluate whether a formal challenge is warranted.
